clue.text: Groups of sailors reported to be making journey

indicators.note: reported means the word for the sailors is said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a ship's crews are groups of sailors

explanation.surface: Ship's companies are said to be setting off on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a pleasure voyage by sea, a kind of journey.

clue.text: The personification of revelry has to cut short supporting business

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes after the word for business

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: has to means must

explanation.surface: Even the spirit of partying must cut back to prop up a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Comus is the Greek god of revelry, subject of Milton's masque.
explanation.definitionFit: Comus is the classical deity of festivity and merrymaking, revelry embodied.

clue.text: Pants maybe like one drowning in NE river?

parts.note: someone drowning has gone under
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham and Sunderland

explanation.surface: Wonders if someone's trousers resemble a person sinking in a Northumbrian river.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage pants are underpants, not trousers, which is why 'maybe' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain pants means underpants, one example of garments worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: Playwright in short piece of fabric wrapped round

indicators.note: in short means the word is cut back, losing its final letter

parts.note: a shawl is a piece of fabric wrapped round the shoulders

explanation.surface: A dramatist briefly swathed in cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: George Bernard Shaw wrote Pygmalion and Saint Joan.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist, author of many celebrated stage works.

clue.text: Pick each straggly plant

indicators.note: straggly suggests something untidy and spread about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to choose every untidy-looking plant in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickpea is a leguminous plant grown for its edible seeds.

clue.text: The man had to admit seven-year problem, being this?

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the contraction for the man had takes in the problem

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had
the seven-year itch is restlessness said to strike a marriage after seven years

explanation.surface: A man confesses the classic restlessness that afflicts husbands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being this?' refers back: the seven-year itch afflicts those who are married.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitched is informal for married, the state in which the seven-year itch is said to arrive.

clue.text: Is not a man mistaken for Messiah able to be seen in one region of Spain?

definitions.text: able to be seen in one region of Spain?

parts.note: can't, cannot, is a way of saying is not able
in Monty Python's Life of Brian the hero Brian is mistaken for the Messiah

explanation.surface: Asks whether a would-be Messiah can be spotted somewhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Monty Python's film Life of Brian is about a man taken for the Messiah.
explanation.definitionFit: Something Cantabrian belongs to Cantabria, a northern Spanish region, so it is found there.

clue.text: Where vehicles may be reclaimed for money

definitions.meaning: a car ... holds towed vehicles until owners pay to recover them

explanation.surface: The place you go to pay to get your towed car back.
explanation.definitionFit: Towed cars are held in a vehicle compound, and the British currency unit is sterling's basic denomination.

clue.text: Notice fellows being imprisoned chaps needing time for reform

indicators.note: being imprisoned means the word for fellows is locked inside the word for notice

parts.note: AD, an advertisement, is a notice
fellows are men
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A notice about men in prison who need their sentences for rehabilitation.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to improve something, a reform or correction.

clue.text: Artist captures film character in something that helps conjure up image

definitions.text: something that helps conjure up image

indicators.note: captures means the artist's letters surround the others

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist
ET is the alien in Spielberg's film
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter depicts a movie figure inside some device that creates pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer in the eye on which a picture is formed.

clue.text: Without delay, heartily try to resolve dispute

indicators.note: heartily asks for only the heart of the word, so its opening pair and closing pair of letters are dropped

parts.note: without delay means immediately

explanation.surface: An urgent, earnest attempt to settle a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' looks like an adverb on 'try' but keeps only the core of IMMEDIATELY, losing IM and LY.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to intervene between parties to bring about a settlement of their quarrel.

clue.text: Fashion certain … to suit monks!

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A fashionable look guaranteed to flatter the brothers in the monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a monk's shaved crown is a fashion that certainly suits monks.
explanation.definitionFit: The tonsure is the shaved patch on the crown of the head traditionally worn by monks.

clue.text: Island that's harsh with temperature dropping

indicators.note: dropping says a letter falls out of the word for harsh

parts.note: harsh means stark

explanation.surface: An island with a severe climate where the thermometer keeps falling.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small island in the Channel Islands group, near Guernsey.

clue.text: Haughty, like charismatic worshippers?

definitions.meaning: charismatic church congregations raise their hands aloft in praise, so they are literally hands-up

explanation.surface: Arrogant, in the manner of a lively evangelical congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: worshippers with their hands held high.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overbearing acts without regard for others, much like a haughty, arrogant person.

clue.text: Ten marbles — different or having similar appearance?

indicators.note: different signals that the letters are made into something else

explanation.surface: Asks whether ten marbles are all distinct or all look alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Resemblant is a rare adjective for resembling, looking alike.

clue.text: Can Democrat keep true as US President?

indicators.note: keep means hold within, so the word for can holds the word for true

parts.note: taken as the word can itself, a tin
true in the sense of flat or even, level

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Democratic politician can stay honest as head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Grover Cleveland, a Democrat, was the 22nd and 24th US President.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland served two non-consecutive terms as American head of state in the 1880s and 1890s.

clue.text: Careful journalist will get this legal protection against piracy

definitions.meaning: a careful journalist gets the copy, the text, correct
the legal right protecting authors from having works reproduced

explanation.surface: A conscientious reporter secures protection against plagiarism.
explanation.walkthrough: Copy is the journalist's text; the first reading splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors hold the exclusive legal right to reproduce their work, which guards against piracy.

clue.text: Bad person has Irish accent, not British

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for British is left out

parts.note: a brogue is a strong Irish accent

explanation.surface: A villain speaks with an Irish lilt rather than an English one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled man, a scoundrel.

clue.text: The egoist getting out of hand is put in a separate place

indicators.note: getting out of hand suggests disorder, so the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A self-centred person who becomes unruly is shut away.
explanation.definitionFit: To ghettoise is to confine or segregate a group in a separate area.

clue.text: Politician's beginning to press for clean-up act

indicators.note: beginning takes just the opening letter of the word for the politician

parts.note: to press for something is to urge it

explanation.surface: A politician starts by demanding a campaign against corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is an abrupt removal of undesirable people, a cleaning-out.

clue.text: What's offered by Superman — entertainment for evermore

indicators.note: the phrase says the letters are given within the words that follow, spanning both

explanation.surface: A superhero film promising everlasting fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival here: a thing that is for evermore.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting for evermore is everlasting, enduring without end.

clue.text: Triple rum Henry imbibed — magical drink?

indicators.note: imbibed means taken in, so the mixed-up letters swallow the abbreviation
rum means odd or strange, so the word beside it is rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry downs a triple measure of rum, an enchanted draught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the old adjective meaning odd, here an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A philtre is a potion with magical powers, especially a love potion.

clue.text: Third of agenda will be covered by meeting in fact

indicators.note: covered by means placed inside the word for meeting

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting

indicators.note: third of picks out the third letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Item three on the agenda will be dealt with at the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Really is an adverb meaning actually, as a matter of truth.

clue.text: Plain Bruce possibly a dissident Aussie?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A plain Australian called Bruce, perhaps a rebel of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruce is the stereotypical Aussie name; Australian republicans dissent from keeping the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian who wants to replace the monarchy with an elected head of state is called a republican.

clue.text: Healthy food will give regular bodily motion!

definitions.meaning: edible seeds such as lentils and beans
the rhythmic beat of the arteries

explanation.surface: Wholesome eating keeps you regular.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at bowel movements; the second sense is the heartbeat felt in the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils and beans are nutritious legumes, and the throb of the arteries is the heartbeat felt at the wrist.

clue.text: They are as one together that's the thing with them

definitions.meaning: a couple in a relationship are said to be an ...
a single thing or article in a list

explanation.surface: A couple who are inseparable, and that is what is notable about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people romantically linked are called an item, and an object or entry on a list is also one.

clue.text: Monsieur to be in France in his unit

parts.note: être is French for to be

explanation.surface: A French gentleman wants to be in his own country's measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' points back to the Frenchman: the metre is the French-born unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: The metre is the base unit of length in the metric system devised in France.

clue.text: A female wants yellow tincture showing up in hairstyle

indicators.note: in a down answer showing up means read upwards, so the heraldic word is turned

parts.note: or is the heraldic tincture gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A woman wants yellow dye to appear in her hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry the tinctures are the colours; or is gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a bushy, rounded style of naturally curly hair.

clue.text: Bitterness shown by relation spurning upper-class lady-killer?

parts.note: gall means bitterness or resentment

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the letter for upper-class is thrown out

parts.note: an aunt is a relation

explanation.surface: A posh relative resentfully rejecting a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is a dashing man attentive to women, a ladies' man, as lady-killer suggests.

clue.text: Socialist-leaning cant spread across English newspaper

indicators.note: spread across means the word for cant goes around the other letters

parts.note: to cant is to tilt or lean, to list
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Left-wing jargon smeared over an English paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cant' looks like hypocritical talk but means a tilt; the FT is the Financial Times, a London paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftist holds left-wing views, inclining towards socialism.

clue.text: Restrictions will have disappeared in a decade of frivolity

definitions.text: Restrictions will have disappeared in a decade of frivolity

parts.words: Restrictions will have disappeared in a decade of frivolity
parts.note: restrictions are ties; with them gone the Roaring years after the Great War were a decade of jazz and fun

explanation.surface: A decade of fun when all the old rules were thrown off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roaring 1920s were the era of flappers and jazz, a famously carefree decade.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1920s are remembered as a period of hedonism, flappers and loosened social constraints.

clue.text: Take care of that lady — ultimately some "gel"!

parts.note: CO, c/o, is the postal abbreviation for care of
her refers to that lady

indicators.note: ultimately takes only the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An instruction to look after a woman, who in the end is quite a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gel' looks like a posh pronunciation of girl, but it is the verb meaning set or stick together.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to come together and form a unified whole, which is what things that cohere do.
